Header: Frankliniella occidentalis Western flower thrips, alfalfa thrips

Prevention: Thrips are tiny insect that can spread viruses on crops.
Use only thrips-free seedlings from certified nurseries.
Mulch with polythene to prevent thrips to pupate in the ground
Conserve natural enemies (predatory thrips, green lacewings, pirate bugs, parasitic wasps and predatory mites) by avoiding pesticides.
Keep old crop fields away from new ones (other vegetables, tobacco + commercial flower plants).
Avoid planting crop next to onions, garlic or cereals as high thrips numbers often build up on these.
Avoid using fields near greenhouses where ornamentals are grown as these act as hosts for the virus and thrips.
Use a fertilizer programme to avoid nutrient deficiencies as thrips prefer those crops.
Monitoring: Monitor regularly for thrips/symptoms from seedlings-harvest.
Shake crop onto paper to monitor.
Thrips usually feed on young lower leaf surfaces, buds, flowers + fruits.
Feeding by adults + immatures causes silvering (silver tiny spots) on leaves, distorts plant growth, deforms flowers.
Floral abortion occurs, fruits are not well- shaped (of poor selling quality).

Direct Control: Daily overhead irrigation (2-5 mm) at midday to reduce pest.
Leaves must dry quickly to avoid diseases.
Use blue/yellow sticky trap to attract + kill adults (8 traps per 0.5 acres).
Use neem-based products, spray once every two weeks if threshold is breached, maxium 3 times.
Spray late afternoon when thrips are active, but so the leaves dry before night.
Beauveria bassiana during late afternoon/after sunset as
UV light may degrade the product.
Check label for dosage as products may differ.
Flood the field after harvest to destroy pupae in the soil.
